claims.text: The formation and persistence of a protective oxide layer in CrFeCoNiX alloys above 900 °C are primarily controlled by the identity of X.
Al has a strong affinity for oxygen.
In CrFeCoNiAl, Al promotes rapid formation of an alumina scale.
The alumina scale formed on the Al-containing alloy is dense and slow-growing.
The alumina scale formed on the Al-containing alloy is highly adherent and resists cracking and spallation.
CrFeCoNiMn and CrFeCoNiSi form mixed oxide scales under the specified exposure conditions.
The mixed oxides formed by the Mn- or Si-containing alloys have higher vacancy diffusion rates than the alumina scale.
Higher vacancy diffusion in the mixed oxides causes defective, less coherent scales.
Defective, less coherent mixed oxide scales are more prone to cracking and spallation.
Al has low diffusivity in the alumina lattice.
The Al-containing system has a strong metal–oxide bond.
Low lattice diffusivity and strong metal–oxide bonding inhibit defect formation and oxide-scale growth.
Formation of a thermodynamically stable, coherent alumina scale is favored in the Al-containing alloy.
Mixed oxide scales on the Mn- or Si-containing alloys have weaker interfacial adherence.
CrFeCoNiAl will form a thinner oxide scale than CrFeCoNiMn or CrFeCoNiSi under identical conditions.
CrFeCoNiAl will exhibit a more coherent and adherent scale with less cracking and spallation than the Mn- or Si-containing alloys.
CrFeCoNiMn and CrFeCoNiSi will form thicker, more discontinuous oxide scales than CrFeCoNiAl.
Greater defect density in the Mn- or Si-containing scales will lead to increased cracking and spallation.
The proposed mechanism applies to both single-phase and multiphase CrFeCoNiX metallic solid solutions above 900 °C.
The multiphase state may alter local oxide-formation mechanisms in ways that are not well understood.
